knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = TRUE)

Work through this file alongside the chapter "Covariance and Correlation" in the book. Keep it in the same folder as your `my_functions.R`.

## The data

Practice hours and test scores for eight people. Each position in `x` goes with the same position in `y`.

```{r data}
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
y <- c(48, 55, 51, 62, 58, 70, 65, 71)
```

## Load your toolbox

```{r load-toolbox}
library(tidyverse)
source("my_functions.R")

all.equal(my_mean(y), mean(y))
all.equal(my_var(y), var(y))
all.equal(my_sd(y), sd(y))
```

You are looking for three `TRUE`s. If you see `could not find function`, finish the toolbox sections in the earlier exercise files first.

## Two distances from the mean

```{r deviations}
dx <- x - my_mean(x)
dy <- y - my_mean(y)

dx
dy
```

### Your turn: the covariance equation

Multiply the two distances for each person, then add up the products and divide by the number of pairs minus one. You should get about 18.86.

```{r covariance-steps}
products <-
sum() /
```

my_covariance(x, y)

### Check it against `cov()`

```{r my-covariance-check}
c(mine = my_covariance(x, y), R = cov(x, y))
all.equal(my_covariance(x, y), cov(x, y))
```

```{r my-covariance-check-2}
a <- c(2, 4, 9)
b <- c(3, 1, 8)

c(mine = my_covariance(a, b), R = cov(a, b))
all.equal(my_covariance(a, b), cov(a, b))
```

What happens if you put the same variable into both inputs?

```{r covariance-is-variance}
c(covariance = my_covariance(x, x), variance = my_var(x))
all.equal(my_covariance(x, x), my_var(x))
```

## Two predictions

Predict each result before you run it, then explain it using deviations from the mean.

```{r predictions}
my_covariance(x * 60, y)
my_correlation(x * 60, y)
my_correlation(x, y + 10)
my_correlation(x, -y)
```

### Check it against `cor.test()`

```{r my-correlation-t-check}
correlation_result <- cor.test(x, y, method = "pearson")
correlation_result

c(mine = my_correlation_t(x, y), R = unname(correlation_result$statistic))
all.equal(my_correlation_t(x, y), unname(correlation_result$statistic))
```

## Try it on real data

Each patient in `sleep` tried both drugs. The rows for the two drugs are in the same patient order, so the two vectors below are paired.

```{r real-data}
drug_1 <- sleep %>% filter(group == 1) %>% pull(extra)
drug_2 <- sleep %>% filter(group == 2) %>% pull(extra)
drug_result <- cor.test(drug_1, drug_2)

c(mine = my_correlation(drug_1, drug_2), R = cor(drug_1, drug_2))
all.equal(my_correlation(drug_1, drug_2), cor(drug_1, drug_2))
all.equal(my_correlation_t(drug_1, drug_2), unname(drug_result$statistic))
```

## Add to your toolbox

1. Open `my_functions.R`.
2. Copy your finished `my_covariance()`, `my_correlation()`, and `my_correlation_t()` into it, under the **Covariance and Correlation** heading. Copy only the functions.
3. Save `my_functions.R`.

Now check that the saved toolbox works on its own. You are looking for three `TRUE`s.

```{r toolbox-check}
rm(list = ls())
source("my_functions.R")

x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
y <- c(48, 55, 51, 62, 58, 70, 65, 71)
result <- cor.test(x, y)

all.equal(my_covariance(x, y), cov(x, y))
all.equal(my_correlation(x, y), cor(x, y))
all.equal(my_correlation_t(x, y), unname(result$statistic))
```

If you see `could not find function`, that function is not in `my_functions.R` yet, or the file was not saved.
